en: Your nap is interrupted by a loud roar.
"Alright, pid noct, here's your toss!"
"Hey Peregrine?
"Lad, we were all in a mood yesterday. We all find... ways to get over it. Don't worry yourself."
"Lass, we were all in a mood yesterday. We all find... ways to get over it. Don't worry yourself."
"Sleep well, gentlemen?
"Tails!"
"Thanks. I was kind of an asshole yesterday, and I don't say it enough, but thanks."
"Yeah, boss?"
"You too, Logus. Thanks for all your help, and sorry for the bad attitude. I'll try to be better."
After an hour or more of staring at the ceiling and becoming increasingly frustrated, you decide to get up quietly and go sit near the fire.
As the two keep trying to outdo one another, their tales grow taller and lewder, and you're almost certain they've begun inventing them.
As you step out of the hallway, you hear voices murmuring quietly.
At some point, you drift off, and when you awake, startled, the morning sun is peeking in through the dirty windows.
Even though you haven't been invited, listening to their tales is extremely diverting, and the hours slip away as quickly for you as the whiskey does for them.
If you've ever seen an orc blush as hard as Logus is blushing, you can't recall. You can probably guess how their game turned out.
It looks as though they got into some kind of fight. Apparently their plans fell through. You decide to try to diffuse their animosity.
It seems your apology has been well-received.
It seems your friends do not think quite so poorly of you after all.

It would have been fun to be invited to their game, but it's clear the two of them have shared something special tonight, and you drift off to sleep with a grin on your face as you recall some of their absurd yarns.
Logus is quite drunk, and he misses catching the coin. It hits the floor and rolls right past your hiding spot.
Logus suddenly stands up and kicks his stool aside, tearing off his clothes as he does.
Logus takes a pre-poured glass of whiskey and drinks it straight to the bottom in one long drag, then puts the glass on the floor and braces his hands against his knees.
Of course, the moment you actually lay down to sleep, you find yourself wide awake.
Peregrine and Logus are avoiding eye contact with one another, and Logus has some visible bruising on his arms.
Peregrine and Logus waste no time getting acquainted with one another's bodies.
Peregrine lifts his drink to his lips, and empties it in one long, decisive swig.
They are definitely up to something, and they do not seem to be pleased with you.
You breathe a heavy sigh of relief. It seems their grand plot against you was simply to cut you out of a drinking game.
You decide to creep closer and listen.
You decide to take this opportunity to escape back to your room before being discovered.
You manage to return to your room without being discovered or waking anybody else.
You sit and listen secretly as Peregrine and Logus share drinks and swap lurid stories of their lewdest escapades.
You spend the rest of your night awake in your room with a weapon in your hand, certain that the two of them are conspiring against you.
A burlap sack lies on the ground--the goblins must have been trying to hide it. It contains a small key and some gold.
A metal shield is positioned neatly inside this chest. Take it with you?
A sturdy wooden portcullis blocks the way. You are currently on the inside, so there should be a way to raise it.

As you begin to tip the vial, a horrible gelatinous blob jumps out and lands on the mechanism with a squelch. It clings to the bottom of the lever and spreads itself out, fizzing all over as it begins to dissolve the rust.
If you had something to take care of the rust, you might be able to pull it without damaging the mechanism.
Most of the vials do not have labels. You have a look at the ones which do--slug salt, rust remover, lamp oil, oak varnish, and bug repellent.
None of these are particularly useful right now...
The fizzing eventually stops. The blob contracts back into its rounded shape, and falls away from the lever.
The lever is now free of rust, and has a noticeable shine. It should be okay to use now.
The mechanism on this lever has rusted over completely. Applying too much force may break off the handle.
The mechanism on this lever has rusted over completely. Attempting to apply too much force may break off the handle.
The tools appear to be quite worn, but the tarps seem fairly clean and in good condition.
These crates are filled with old iron tools, tarps, and vials of liquid. Do you want to take a closer look?
Would you like to use the rust remover?
You decide to take the rust remover.
You open the vial of rust remover and kneel down by the lever.
You see a gold key laying on the desk. Take it with you?
As you recruit more people, don't forget to keep at least a few focused on utility skills. They'll come in handy later.
Bato's abilities are heavily focused toward his utility stats. This makes him a poor combatant, but an excellent worker.
I... am alive, right? You're going to let me go, aren't you?
Is somebody there? Please, let me go! I don't want to die!
It looks as though the jewel you found will fit into the indentation here. Will you insert it?
It looks as though the passage forward has been barricaded with debris.
Oh thank God! There used to be a few of us, but they've dragged the others off to who knows where. I'm the last one alive.
Somebody has abandoned a pack full of provisions here. They are old, but quite edible.
The cell door should now be unlocked.
The debris is loose, and you manage to move it without hurting yourself.
The lid moved, but not enough to get at the contents.
The lid on this coffer is extraordinarily heavy. It will take a good deal of work to open it.
The small green jewel fits neatly into the top of the pedestal and immediately bursts into intense flames.
There is a worn impression in the tip of this pedestal. It looks like an object is meant to fit inside.
You decide to hold on to the jewel for now.
You have, however, made a good deal of noise. If anything is out there, it knows you are coming.
There is a small pillow book in the drawer of this end table.
Borgnina sighs loudly.
Inside one of these crates, you find an unbroken bottle of liquor. It was probably a cheap vintage back when this place was in use, but it's ancient now.

The sign reads - "Tonight's special - braised lamb!"

The sign is so badly weathered, you're certain it can't be recent.
Peeking over the edge, it looks like the floor below is weak enough to be broken by the water-filled barrel. Push the barrel down?
The chain in the winch could be lowered if the rubble from the floor below could be cleared out.
The chest has been opened recently, the contents plundered.
The lever appears to be stuck in place, and does not seem to budge one bit. It doesn't look like you'll be able to unlock the door connected to this switch.
You climb down to where you heard the voices come from earlier, but it appears they have left.

You unwind the chain with the winch, lowering it down into the darkness below. Once the winch reaches the end of the chain, you give it a few tugs to make sure it can carry your weight before lowering yourself down.
It reads : Prove that you have power to destroy Rakanratep.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Spark Soul upon the pedestal?
The pedestal is marked with carvings of twisting flames. There is an inscription on the very top.
You decide to hold on to the Spark Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Spark Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
It reads : This labyrinth houses violence incarnate, and is meant for no other.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Marauder Soul upon the pedestal?
The pedestal is engraved with a large warning.
You decide to hold on to the Marauder Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Marauder Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
The grinding of stone upon stone rumbles in the distance.
This scroll appears to mark the path to the exit. You should be able to use this to return outside easily.
Amid the bits of refuse and fluff, you spy something small and sparkling.
He snaps his fingers and the air goes taut.
There is a book here that seems out of place, as though it's been stuffed into the shelf quickly.
There is a key on the top of this end table.
There's a rock against the side of the manor here.
You should be able to drop from here to the floor below. The drop is not far.
A dreadful, repulsive energy emanates from this eerie stone fist.
A pair of heavy iron doors block the way. They appear to be unlocked, but simply opening them might be difficult.
Did you get turned around? You seem to have come out at the same place you went in.

Emergency Exit

Pull lever to open.
Foreman's Room
If you had a rope, you would probably be able to climb down.
It looks as though there used to be something implanted in the floor here, but it's been ripped out.
Open the door?

Spelunking Area

Please observe safety precautions. Strictly no access without appropriate clothing and equipment.
The Holy Pickaxe you found earlier is throbbing in your hand.
The chest is filled with scrolls and blueprints. There is a small compartment at one side, which houses a key.
The chest opens easily, but there is nothing inside.
The clamp separates into two parts, and falls away.
The lever will not budge. A heavy, metal clamp has been fitted at the bottom.
The passage seems to loop back on itself.
The pickaxe shatters into fragments and the stone fist cracks open, revealing a modest golden amulet.
There appears to be something contained within it, but getting too close overwhelms you with an unholy sense of nausea.
There is a map pinned open on the table, which shows the layout of the mine.
There is an iron anchor set into the floor here.
This door appears to lack any kind of handle, but you can see a latch near the top.
Try as you might, the chest will not open.
Try opening the doors?
Use your rope to climb down?
You can't be sure, but the map feels unfinished. That, or whoever started the mining efforts here didn't get very far.
You lean against the doors and give them a final push.
You lift the pickaxe high above your head and bring it down hard against the stone fist.
You notice that there is a keyhole on the side of the clamp. Would you like to try using the Foreman's Key?
A moment later, the lid pops open, and you find to your disappointment that your tampering has released some kind of failsafe. The contents of the chest have been destroyed with acid.
Deftly, you finesse the chest's lock and pop the top open.
Something went wrong. The Adonis shatters into a million shards of obsidian, and the mana in the room goes still.
The Adonis shatters into a million shards of obsidian, and the mana in the room goes still.
The air in the room grows thin, and one by one, you and your band drop to the floor.
The desk is piled high with books. Whoever was studying here must have been rather frantic about it.
The journal on the table is left open to the final entry.
The mana converged briefly and then went wild, lashing your mind.
The mechanism snaps shut, catching your skin painfully. You catch the faint whiff of something acrid, and a vapour begins to leak from the seams in the lid.
This altar is laid out in a purposeful fashion. It looks as though something is meant to be placed here as part of the ritual.
This chest has a complex mechanical lock with no apparent place to insert a key. You'll have to disable it the hard way.
Use the Devil Adonis to complete the ritual with the crystals in this configuration?
With a spine-chilling howl, the very fabric of being is split open, and a frothing gateway is laid open.
You focus the threads of mana onto the Devil Adonis. It glitters intensely for a moment.
You gently position the Devil Adonis in the centre of the altar and attempt to complete the ritual.
"Repeat offenders will undergo corporal punishment.
A horrible smell lingers in the air...
Above you is a narrow hole in the ceiling which leads above ground. It's too high to reach from here, but you are certain that's where the gallows are.
Behind the chest, you notice something with a long handle resting against the wall.
Next to the stack of papers is a small wooden box. The town's emblem has been etched into it.
On top of a pile of unused envelopes you notice a silver-rimmed monocle, which emits a faint glow.
That swing was not so mighty.
The Marauder Soul you are carrying throbs in your hand, clearly reacting to the pedestal.
The chest contains a few tools used for grounds maintenance, but they all appear to be worn and rusted.
The chest contains a neatly stacked pile of trading permit applications. Nearly all of the aplications appear to have a line drawn across them, as if to suggest they have expired or been voided.
The crate is lined with jugs of fine, local ale. It is unlikely that anyone is going to come back for these, considering the town has been overrun by monsters, so you decide to help yourself.
The gallows show no sign of recent use, and appear to be partially dismantled.
The jail warden must have been hiding a stash of seized goods down here.
The top of the pedestal is covered in streaks of dried blood, and the stone is gouged and slashed, as if by the slavering jaws of a terrible creature.
There is a palpable aura of ferocious violence and desperate hunger emanating from the bloodstained pedestal.
This cabinet holds a variety of old writing equipment.
This section of wall has been securely boarded up, but you might be able to smash through using the Warhammer.
This section of wall has been securely boarded up.
This stone pedestal emits a strange light.
Try and break through?
Unleashing the most savage war cry you can muster, you bring down your hammer against the wall.
You hold the hammer with a firm grip, and prepare a mighty swing.
You make an offering of the Marauder Soul, the culmination of many instruments of death.
You notice, however, that there is an open hatch in the flooring, which leads down into a body-wide pit. There is an unpleasant smell coming from below...
You open up the wooden box to find a large, oddly shaped key. Its handle also bears the town's emblem--engraved into the handle. You decide to take the key with you for now.
You sense an eerie presence behind you.
Your offering is consumed in a nauseating flash, and amid the ruins of the pedestal sits an axe, old and weathered, with an uneven glint, as though there were blood folded into the steel itself.
A support pillar. It looks as though it has been erected somewhat recently, and is holding the weight of the warped roof.
Try as you might, you can't seem to gain enough leverage to push the pillar out of place.
Without the support pillars in place, the weight of the collapsing building starts to shift.
You might be able to knock it out if you can push it hard enough.
You open the chest with your mind, and surprisingly, without  your intervention, a knife floats out of the chest and toward you, hilt-first, as if answering a summons.
You push the support pillar out of place, and the heavy roof groans in protest.
It seems that nobody else will be using that passage.
The tunnel is starting to collapse!
You'll have to move single-file through this tunnel. It doesn't look particularly safe, so you decide to go one at a time.
The zombie is particularly malodorous today.
Captain Logus sits here alone, smoke trailing from a pipe clenched in his teeth. When he notices your approach he stands and adjusts his hat.
Logus scans your group and folds his arms across his chest, frowning.
Logus takes a deep breath and gazes up at the sky for a long moment.
"...my fault... underground... nearby. I hear... water... can't keep..."
"Kirilo and I were... attacked. They drugged us and...
"Well this day is turning out to be far more interesting than I thought."
Kirilo and Shapiro need your help!
That was a close call.
There are obvious signs of a struggle, and heavy footprints. You follow them and eventually discover the entrance to an underground structure of some kind.
They've both been badly poisoned, but it looks like the poison is not lethal, and they should recover given a little time.
This must be where Kirilo and Shapiro were taken.
You break off and give the woodland surrounding the old home a quick search.
You carefully follow the footsteps of your friends and spot the place where they were attacked.
You guide your friends out of the dungeon and send for help from your stronghold.
Do you want to pass the key through the grate?
Hey! Hey you! Down here, under the grate.
I don't know what you did, but you made the exit close off, and now I'm trapped in here. There's a keyhole, but I can't find any key that fits it on this side.
Perfect. I'll go see if this works.
See if there's a key over there and pass it through.
This switch does not move. It appears to be locked into position.
Well, hurry up and go find it!
Well? Did you find it?
You pass the key down into the grate.
Despite your bangs and bruises, however, the path is now clear.
Greave steps forward, his knuckles tight on the grip of his sword. When he turns to speak to you, his face is stone cold.
Some sort of torture device.
The bricks collapse on top of you!
The bricks here are loosely piled, and not mortared together. You might be able to tear them down with a little elbow grease.
The wall comes down, revealing a path into the adjacent cell.
Judging by the size of this footlocker, it appears to have belonged to someone important, probably the guard captain. The lock on this chest still holds fast.
There are many bottles in this crate, most of them empty. You do, however, find one that is still sealed and full of very expensive liquor.
There is a key sitting on this table.
This appears to have been a soldier's footlocker.
You play with the lock until you get a cramp in your elbow, but to no avail. Best take a breath and start over.
You skillfully pop the tumblers open and the chest gives up its treasures.

After a short while, your vision becomes hazy, and you 
succumb to your tiredness.
After dropping a few rocks into the hole, you notice there is no sound of impact.
Empty out the sack?
Large pieces of debris from the broken walls are littered across the ledge. It might be safer to push them off, rather than try to step over them.
The campfire has gone out.
The wall has completely collapsed here - you can see outside. It's a long way down...
The water inside the barrel is cool and fresh. You scoop up a handful and splash your face with it.
The way forward is now clear.
There are a few bottles of vintage soda laying inside.
There is a nice, warm campfire here. It crackles gently in the breeze.
There seems to be no way around it.
There's a small silver key on top of the cabinet.
This cabinet is covered in dust. The drawer seems to be locked.
This chest is teetering off the edge...
This sack is made of a thick, densely woven material. You pick it up, and a pleasant jingling sound comes from inside.
Try removing the rubble?
Well, so much for that.
Whatever this room was, it's now a balcony.
